prs.title: fix(Toolbar): keep focus on the clicked button
prs.author: arba-octo
prs.body:
Fix Toolbar restoring focus to the previous button when another button is clicked after leaving the toolbar. Preserve keyboard focus restoration and add regression coverage.

Closes #10934

prs.title: fix: prevent stacked Sheet backdrop flashes in Firefox
prs.author: dagemawinegash
prs.body:
Closes #10924.

## Summary

Keeps the bottom Sheet's backdrop dimmed while nested sheets open and close in Firefox. Each sheet gets a stable timeline name from its existing ID, independent of its stack index, following the approach suggested in the issue. Backdrop, swipe and descendant stack animations use these names; stack indexes continue to control order and styling.

## 📝 Test Instructions

1. Run `yarn start-parcel3` and open **React Aria Components → Sheet → Sheet Stacking**. In Firefox, enable `layout.css.scroll-driven-animations.enabled` in `about:config` and reload.
2. Open sheet 1, open and close sheet 2, then repeat with three stacked sheets and a freshly reopened outer sheet. The bottom backdrop should remain dimmed throughout nested opening and closing.

Validation:

- `yarn test packages/react-aria-components/test/Sheet.test.js --runInBand`: 65 passed. Both new unit regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward.
- The two new browser regressions pass in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox with view timelines enabled. Both fail on the original source in Firefox at the backdrop-opacity assertion.
- Full browser suite: 464 passed, 71 skipped, two TokenField word-deletion failures. Both failures reproduce on unchanged source.
- Full unit suite: 7,894 passed, 16 skipped, 16 failures across four unrelated suites. The failures reproduce on unchanged source and concern Windows locale/path handling and the codemod fixture.

prs.title: fix(useSliderState): avoid repeated onChange calls for unchanged values
prs.author: isihussain
prs.body:
Closes #10950

## Summary

In controlled sliders (`value` + `onChange`), once a dragged thumb moves to a new value, subsequent pointer moves within that same step repeatedly call `onChange` with the unchanged value until the drag ends.

### Cause
In `useSliderState`, `valuesRef` retains the array passed to the last `setValues`. When the parent re-renders with the new controlled value, `useControlledState` stores the new array passed from `props.value`. On subsequent pointer moves within the same step, `replaceIndex` returns `valuesRef.current` unchanged, but that array is not the same reference that `useControlledState` holds. Consequently, `useControlledState`'s `Object.is` check fails and fires `onChange` again on every pointer move.

### Solution
Add an early return in `updateValue` when `valuesRef.current[index] === value`. If the thumb at the given index is already at the snapped step value, no state update is needed, preventing redundant `onChange` calls and unnecessary re-renders.

## 📝 Test Instructions

Added regression test in `packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js`:
- Renders `useSliderState` in controlled mode with a spy on `onChange`.
- Drags thumb to value 50 and asserts `onChange` was called once.
- Triggers another move at value 50 and asserts `onChange` was not called again (still called 1 time total).

prs.title: fix: allow Mod+A to select ComboBox input text while multi-select menu is open
prs.author: mangeshraut712
prs.body:
## Summary
When a multi-select ComboBox menu is open, Mod+A was handled by list selection (`selectAll`) which ignored the selection change but still called `preventDefault`, so the input could not select its filter text.

Set `disallowSelectAll: true` on the ComboBox list collection so Mod+A falls through to the browser default (select input text).

Closes #10866

## Test plan
- [x] RAC ComboBox test: Mod+A with multi-select popover open does not select all options and does not `preventDefault` on the input keydown

prs.title: fix: declare optional React type peers for published packages
prs.author: Sophran-fbj
prs.body:
Closes #10940

## Summary

In pnpm's global virtual store, the published declarations can resolve `react` to its untyped JavaScript entry even when the application has installed `@types/react`. This loses contextual typing for callbacks such as `Button.onKeyDown`.

Declare `@types/react` as an optional peer in `react-aria-components`, `react-aria`, `react-stately`, and `@react-types/shared`. The range `^16.8.0 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0` follows the supported React major versions. The optional flag keeps JavaScript-only installs working without React type packages. Update the workspace lockfile accordingly.

Also exclude optional peers from the workspace constraint that propagates required peers. Otherwise, these declarations cause the constraint to require many dependent workspaces to declare the type peer as a required dependency. Required-peer propagation is unchanged. Manifest key ordering was normalized by the repository formatter.

Prepared with AI assistance (Codex), including implementation, local validation, and this description.

prs.title: fix: propagate useTreeData mutations through falsy parent keys
prs.author: raunakpandey1
prs.body:
Closes #10907

## Summary

Editing a descendant under a parent keyed by `0` or `''` updates the lookup map but leaves stale nodes in the returned tree. For example, `update('child', ...)` changes `getItem('child')` while `items` retains the old value; moving that child to the root can leave it in both locations.

The intent is for mutations to produce a consistent immutable tree for every valid string or numeric parent key. The ancestor reconstruction loop now checks for null/undefined rather than truthiness. This keeps traversal going through valid falsy keys while retaining the root sentinel behavior. Regression tests exercise update, removal and selection cleanup, insertion, and moving to the root under both key types, including an ancestor above the affected parent and preservation of the previous tree snapshot.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with source investigation, implementation, regression tests, validation, and this PR. The author-understanding checklist item is left unchecked for the human contributor to verify.

prs.title: fix(useDateSegment): don't crash when 12-hour time has no day period
prs.author: mangeshraut712
prs.body:
Closes #10833

`DateField`, `TimeField`, and `DatePicker` throw while rendering when the locale is `fr-CM`. `useDateSegment` formats a 12-hour time on every segment to learn the AM/PM strings, then reads `dayPeriod.value`. For `fr-CM`, ICU returns only an hour part, so that read throws. A date-only field crashes too, because the lookup is not limited to the day-period segment.

The field should render. If a locale has no AM/PM marker, typing a period should simply be unavailable.

The lookup now treats a missing `dayPeriod` as an empty string, and keystrokes and composition events ignore that empty string so it is not selected as a period. Locales that do include AM/PM are unchanged: the first letter still selects the period. The strings are still resolved for every segment, because composition input uses them to recognize letter keys outside the day-period segment. Happy to move that lookup behind `segment.type === 'dayPeriod'` if you would prefer.

This change was prepared with an AI assistant, following AGENTS.md.

prs.title: fix: preserve locale-specific Arabic number separators
prs.author: itsrayeedscodespace
prs.body:
Fixes #10936

## Summary

Numbers formatted for Sindhi and related Arabic-digit locales must retain their native decimal and grouping meanings when parsed. For example, `sd` formats 1234.5 as `١٬٢٣٤.٥`; the existing substitutions can turn its decimal point into grouping and produce 12345.

Apply Arabic keyboard alternatives when the native decimal is U+066B, regardless of the native grouping character. This preserves comma and U+060C decimal aliases in Swedish and Norwegian Arabic-digit input, whose grouping character is a non-breaking space, while keeping Sindhi/Punjabi/Urdu native separators intact. No separator-order or digit-count guessing is introduced.

After native grouping separators are removed, reject a remaining ASCII period whenever it is not the locale's decimal separator, for every numbering system. This keeps parsing consistent with partial validation for inputs such as French `1.000` and Persian `۱.۲۳۴`, and prevents invalid pasted punctuation from replacing the current NumberField value.

The review follow-up in `d6077f748` removes the Arabic-only restriction on that check and the U+066C grouping restriction on decimal aliases. Tests are split into native blur/increment behavior, invalid-paste rejection, and decimal-alias acceptance. The Polish plural-form fixture now uses its native `1,1 roku`; a separate regression explicitly rejects `1.1 roku`.
